question: When difference between compound and simple interest for three years is ₹228 at 4% interest per annum, the principal is ₹______
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for CI and SI difference for 3 years is D = P × (R/100)² × (300 + R)/100.

Here, D = 228 and R = 4%.

⇒ 228 = P × (4/100)² × (304/100)

⇒ 228 = P × (1/625) × (76/25)

⇒ P = (228 × 15625) ÷ 76 = 3 × 15625

**∴ The correct answer is ₹46875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ 228 = P × (4/100)² × (300 + 4)/100

⇒ 228 = P × (1/25)² × (304/100)

⇒ 228 = P × (1/625) × (76/25)

⇒ P = (228 × 625 × 25) ÷ 76

⇒ P = 3 × 15625

⇒ P = 46875

**∴ The correct answer is ₹46875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference for 2 Years

The difference between CI and SI for exactly 2 years is given by the formula: D = P × (R/100)².

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years, the effective compound interest rate is calculated as [R + R + (R² ÷ 100)]% of the principal.

Tree Method for CI

A visual technique that clearly separates interest on principal (the simple interest part) and interest on previous interest (the difference part) across different years.
